summary:
How Not to Die on Mars turns scientific data that often feels tedious into an interactive experience where every decision has consequences. It is a 10-chapter, 7-ending web-based visual novel aimed at young audiences aged 13 and older that seeks to build literacy about Mars and space exploration in an engaging way.

The player takes on the role of an astronaut who must complete a 3.5 to 4 km walk through the boxwork area of Mount Sharp, in Gale Crater. Zinn-IA, who lives inside the spacesuit's tablet, displays a map with five data layers from different NASA missions: optical imagery (MRO HiRISE), elevation (MGS MOLA), terrain firmness (Mars Odyssey THEMIS), minerals (MRO CRISM and Curiosity), and radiation and weather (Curiosity RAD and REMS). Using this information, the player decides which route to take, where to collect scientific samples, and how to respond to a solar alert. Five survival bars and a clock shift after each choice and determine whether the astronaut returns home, remains on Mars, or does not survive.

Learning to read a scientific map of Mars is, literally, the key to surviving.
details:
Play it: https://demo-visual-novel.vercel.app/

Code: https://github.com/VanessaA1A/ComoNoMorirEnMarte

WHAT IT DOES

How Not to Die on Mars is a web-based visual novel that places the scientific map of a Martian route at the center of a story. Players do not merely read data: they use data to make decisions, and those decisions determine whether they survive. The player is an astronaut wearing the Nicaraguan emblem who walks from Base Aurora to the boxwork ridges of Mount Sharp (Gale Crater) and back before the return vehicle launches.

HOW IT WORKS

- 10 chapters (journey, surface walk and return), 76 scenes, 7 endings and 154,197 possible paths. Branches diverge and reconverge in a diamond structure, and state flags carry forward to later chapters.

- Zinn-IA, an AI shaped like a zinnia (the first flower to bloom aboard the ISS in 2016), explains each datum in one or two lines before every decision and changes expression with the scene.

- The tablet minimap expands to five toggleable layers: Optical (HiRISE), Elevation (MOLA), Terrain (THEMIS), Minerals (CRISM + Curiosity) and Radiation (RAD/REMS). Layers were exported from JPL Mars Trek with identical bounds so they overlay accurately.

- Five survival bars (oxygen, battery, nutrition, suit integrity, radiation) and a launch clock update after every choice. Example: THEMIS reveals loose sand, so the sandy shortcut risks getting stuck and drains oxygen.

- Each ending shows which choices moved the bars and which map layer would have prevented the problem.

- Survival Guide side panel with rules, layers, unlockable fact cards and sources; a global MOLA map of Mars with real landing sites and unlockable destinations.

BENEFITS AND IMPACT

Designed for youth aged 13+, teachers, museums, astronomy clubs and science fairs in Nicaragua and the region. It shows how scientific data drive real decisions, sparks interest in STEM and builds data literacy: comparing sources, recognizing limitations and telling confirmed findings from potential signals. Spanish-language access and a Nicaraguan protagonist bring space exploration closer to youth who rarely see themselves represented in it.

TOOLS AND TECHNOLOGIES

React and Vite (frontend), Node.js and Express (API), PostgreSQL (saves and statistics), react-leaflet and Leaflet (layered map), JSON chapter files with an automated script validator, and a path simulator. Visual Studio Code, Git and Jira. Deployed on Vercel. Custom pixel-art sprites by the team; AMORIA and FORCED SQUARE typefaces.

CREATIVITY

Most resources present Mars data to be read; this game presents data to be used. Players zoom from the global map (MOLA) to Gale Crater (CTX) to the walking route (HiRISE), learning why global maps are not enough for a surface walk. Expressive characters, chosen name and pronouns, an aurora-inspired visual identity and multiple endings make learning science a way to win.

FACTORS WE CONSIDERED

- Scientific accuracy: no data enters the game without a source; inaccurate figures from early notes were corrected.

- Balance: across all paths, random play yields 61% good, 24% intermediate and 15% fatal endings; ignoring the map leads to the worst outcomes.

- Limitations: MOLA and THEMIS are coarse at walking scale and HiRISE/CRISM coverage is partial; each fact card states its limitation. Bar values are game balance, justified by NASA data.

- Accessibility: runs in the browser with no login and saves progress locally if the API is unreachable.

- Zinn-IA's dialogue is pre-scripted and verified; the game does not use live generative AI
